author: Mark Delaney
description:
An official Phasmophobia movie is on the way; we learned as much last summer. But what if I said you could watch something quite like Kinetic's ghostbusting co-op game right now? 

That's the elevator pitch I bring you, fellow horror fans, less than two weeks out from Halloween. The movie is Never After Dark, a gorgeously shot, cleverly creepy ghost story that Phasmophobia fans shouldn't miss.

Never After Dark tells the story of Airi, a young woman who can commune with ghosts. She works as a traveling intermediary between the dead and the living, convincing spirits to move on and freeing residents from their hauntings. But on her latest gig, she discovers
title: While You Wait For The Phasmophobia Movie, Don’t Miss This Hidden Gem

author: Ben Janca
description:
Watch us fight though 27 layers of a later game dungeon in Stupid Never Dies with Go Nuts Mode turned on. You play as a Zombie who can "Style Eat" enemies and gain their abilities after turning into them.

You'll get to see multiple environments and watch us play as a good number of monsters while leveling up and becoming strong enough to even one shot some bosses.
title: Stupid Never Dies – 26 Minute Full Dungeon Run Gameplay

author: Dave Irwin
description: Let’s face it, if you are a Castlevania fan or just love metroidvania games in general, you’re probably sinking your teeth into Belmont’s Curse. And why not? After all, it just got a glowing review from our own Steve Watts, and like plenty of the rest of you, I’ve also been eagerly waiting for a new Castlevania adventure for over a decade. One indie team in particular seems keen to grab your attention once your time with Belmont's Curse is over, having recently released a demo for their Castlevania-adjacent roguelike. That game is Draftula, which asks, "What if Dracula commissioned you to build his labyrinthine castle?"
title: After Beating Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse, Help Dracula Rebuild In This Awesome Roguelike

author: Kevin Knezevic
description:
A new Pokemon is landing soon in Pokemon Go. The meteorite Minior is making their debut in the mobile game beginning October 19, but you won't encounter them like a typical Pokemon.

Rather than periodically spawning in the wild, Minior's appearance is fittingly tied to meteor showers. The celestial Pokemon will only spawn on certain evenings when a real-world meteor shower is taking place, so you'll need to fire up the game on specific nights if you want to catch a glimpse of the new monster.

To help you add the falling star to your collection, here are some tips on how to catch Minior, including a schedule of upcoming meteor showers, how to change Minior's form, and whether the meteorite Pokemon can be shiny.
title: How To Get Minior In Pokemon Go

author: Cameron Koch
description:
World of Warcraft: Forever is riding high thanks to its popular beta and upcoming launch, but retail WoW's Midnight expansion feels like it's in a state of crisis by comparison.

The two different versions of WoW couldn't be in more different places. Forever seems to be extremely popular, with Blizzard developers commenting how its beta is breaking records. Blizzard itself has also been more communicative regarding Forever than ever before, with weekly podcasts diving into community topics, forum posts addressing various issues, and frequent updates addressing balance problems and bugs.

Midnight seems to be in the opposite corner. Its latest content update, patch 12.1.5, went live October 13. In addition to new story quests that
title: WoW: Forever Is Soaring, But Midnight Is Struggling

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 releases this week, and with gaming consoles and capable PC rigs now more expensive than ever, you might be wondering if there is another way to play.

Thankfully, there is, but there are a few things you need to know before jumping in.

How to play MW4 without a console or PC

With Game Pass:

Modern Warfare 4 is not included with Xbox Game Pass this year, but if you're a subscriber you can leverage the "stream your own game" program to play it that way, after purchasing it outright.

This isn't locked away to any specific tier of Game Pass, either. You can subscribe to Game Pass Essential, Premium, or Ultimate to stream MW4.
title: You Don’t Need An Expensive Console Or High-End PC To Play Call Of Duty: Modern Warfare 4

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
British actor Rahul Kohli (Saros, Midnight Mass) has a pitch for a new L.A. Noire game, and it sounds pretty great. Speaking to BAFTA Games, Kohli said he would like to see the franchise return with a spinoff that takes players through different time periods, as a cop, as they investigate different crimes.

One such setting coul
title: This LA Noire Spinoff Idea Sounds Incredible

author: Gabe Gurwin
description:
Saros is a phenomenal sci-fi shooter, and it currently stands as my favorite game of 2026. If you've been waiting for the right time to play it--or to play it again--then developer Housemarque has some good news. The new Zenith update is now available for free, adding a boss rush and difficulty options that should appeal to both newcomers and seasoned veterans.

First up, the boss rush. Dubbed "Overlord Rush," the mode comes with its own dedicated leaderboards and tasks you with taking out a series of the game's bosses. Rather than starting on the first boss and fighting uninterrupted to the very end, they're divided into separate "sets" that each contain three fights. Overlord Rush is available via the Primary robot in the main hub area.
title: Saros Gets Boss Rush And Tons Of Difficulty Options With Zenith Update

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Star Wars has had no shortage of breakout alien stars over the decades--from Chewbacca in the original trilogy to Grogu from The Mandalorian--but in Star Wars: Galactic Racer, that honor belongs to Biddy Blas. Who is Biddy Blas? A hotshot racer in the game, with an ego the size of a Death Star and a voice that sounds like a TIE Fighter fueled by nightmares—that's who Biddy Blas is. And in real life, the man behind the voice is none other than indie UK wrestler and actor Richard Summers-Calvert, who is down to "scrib doon" some autographs from fans.

Performing under the name "The Spectacular Tw*t" Charles Crowley, Summers-Calvert has popped up in multiple pro wrestling promotions, including a recent appearance in Ring of Honor. The actor and wrestler says he's been humbled by Biddy Blas's popularity since he was introduced in Star Wars: Galactic Racer.

"I could tell Biddy Bl
title: Star Wars: Galactic Racer’s Biddy Blas Is Voiced By A Sinister Circus Ringmaster Pro Wrestler, And This Makes Sense

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
This year has seen the launch of two Star Wars games, with each one offering a new take on a galaxy far (far!) away. Bit Reactors' Star Wars Zero Company puts its best XCOM foot forward with an aggressive take on turn-based tactics, while Fuse Games' Star Wars Galactic Racer has been hailed for its superb roguelite racing, slick presentation, and the delightful Biddy Blas. Both games have been well received by critics and fans alike, and Lucasfilm Games has been paying attention to the success these independent studios have achieved.

"It very much is part of the strategy," Lucasfilm Games VP Douglas Reilly said to
title: Star Wars Games Could Get More Interesting As Lucasfilm Looks Beyond The Big Studios

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Liquid Swords, the Swedish developer behind the crime game Samson, is closing up shop. Founder Christofer Sundberg confirmed this after bankruptcy reports emerged, stating directly, "Liquid Swords is closing."

Samson launched on PC in April, but the console edition for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S that released in September "did far better," Sundberg said. However, he admitted that, "It wasn't enough to save the studio."

At the same time, Samson might have a future after Liquid Swords closes up shop, the executive said.
title: Open-World Crime Game Samson Did Better On Console But Not Enough To Save Its Developer From Shutting Down

author: Tauriq Moosa
description:
With the recently released Control Resonant, Remedy Entertainment returns to its weird Control universe of teleporting toy ducks, nightmarish creatures, and explosive action, all of which is grounded by a deeply personal central story. But when considering its predecessor, Control, I was struck by just how much this sequel not only differs from the first game, but deliberately inverts or twists what players previously experienced--much as the central Big Bad does to the entire borough of Manhattan. 

Control Resonant begins with our protagonist Dylan, barefoot and in dire need of a shave, awakening from a seven-year coma. With his sister--the series' former main character, Jesse Faden--missing and Control's Oldest House now a crime scene of corpses, Dylan finally leaves the building he’s been imprisoned in for over two decades. He finds a mostly empty Manhattan, cut off from the world, along with the remna
title: Control Resonant Is Everything The First Game Wasn’t, And That’s Why It Works

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Battlefield Studios has released a statement regarding Battlefield 6 after players came together to point out oddities and irregularities with some of the game's newest cosmetics, leading many to openly wonder whether they were the result of generative AI.

The developer’s statement admits mistakes with some of the newly released cosmetics, but it did not say whether genAI played a role.

Battlefield Studios said it's aware of the "conversation, memes, and candid feedback" about some of Battlefield 6's new skins and cosmetic items. In particular, fans pointed out that a McNeil skin says "SECUTY" on the shoulder instead of "SECURITY." Battlefield Studios is planning to release an update to address this with the
title: Battlefield 6 Dev Owns Up To Mistakes With Strange-Looking Cosmetics, But Stays Silent On Possible AI Use

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Season 2 officially launches tomorrow on Netflix, and while the show features a new cast, it also includes one familiar face: veteran game designer Hideo Kojima, who'll cameo as Hideyoshi Oshima in the series.

In Cyberpunk 2077, Oshima plays a braindance producer from Tokyo who wants to create BD experiences that are emotionally resonant with viewers, rather than the more salacious media that made the technology so popular. Modeled after and voiced by Kojima, Oshima pops up in the Konpeki Plaza during the "Heist" mission. Later in the game, players can also find a Bridge Baby Pod Easter egg, a reference to his game Death Stranding.
title: Hideo Kojima Returns To Night City For Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Season 2

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
YouTube star Mr. Beast, who has more than 500 million subscribers on that platform alone, is publishing a Call of Duty video today, October 19, to mark the release of Modern Warfare 4. He teased the video online, saying it's going to be "one of the biggest COD videos of all time."

He also pointed out how he started his YouTube career by posting Call of Duty videos, so it's a full-circle moment for him.

The video appears to be focused around MW4's updated DMZ mode, as a title screen in the video references someth
title: Mr. Beast Teases A Huge Call Of Duty Video Focused On DMZ With Real-Life Content Creators

author: Ben Janca
description:
Faraway is a randomly-generated, minimalistic and demanding, arcade-puzzle game about a shooting star that designs constellations to stay alive. With immersive realtime visuals and interactive music, it’s a game of long-term mastery. You can play in quick bites or hours-long sessions, making it the perfect game to revisit for years to come.

Created single-handedly by game designer, creative coder, and musician Steph Thirion, creator of the cult game Eliss, Faraway is an immersive minimalistic game of deep expressive play, made for discovery, replay, and long-term mastery.

Faraway is coming November 5th to PC (via Steam and the Epic Games Store), Nintendo Switch, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox X|S.
title: Faraway – Official Release Date Reveal Trailer

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
After more than a decade of development, developer Steph Thirion's chill sci-fi game has a release date of locked in. GameSpot can exclusively reveal that Faraway will launch on November 5 for PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and Switch consoles.

See on Steam

Designed to be a tour of the cosmos that you can play with just one button, Faraway was first announced all the way back in 2010, and it follows a shooting star on its journey across the cosmos.  Billed as an endless procedurally generated arcade game, the goal is to create constellations on your trek across the stars, using their gravity to slingshot your way to new destinations and keep your cosmic traveler fueled
title: After 16 Years, Chill Sci-Fi Game Faraway Has A Release Date

author: Aaron Down
description:
Historically, the first time you’d step into a World of Warcraft dungeon as part of The Alliance is The Deadmines. However, World of Warcraft: Forever introduces a new low-level instance called The Hall of Thanes that dishes out blue quality gear like candy on Halloween, getting your character off to a flying start. It’s effectively the Alliance version of Ragefire Chasm, making it the perfect spot to dust off your mechanical cobwebs if it’s been a hot minute, or learn fundamentals if you’re a beginner dungeoneer.

Here, we’ll take you through everything you need to know about WoW: Forever's Hall of Thanes. This includes how to get there, how to clear all five of its associated quests, boss strategies, and, of course, a full rundown of all the juicy loot you can acquire. Based on its difficulty, we’d recommend abstaining from HoT until you reach level 14. The extra spells from this miles
title: WoW: Forever Hall of Thanes Dungeon Guide – Quests, Map, Bosses, and Loot

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
It's that time of month when Xbox updates the Game Pass library, and, as usual, a few more games are leaving the subscription service in a few weeks. On October 31, you can say goodbye to 8 more games, including a few LucasArts classics, a diggy-diggy blast of co-op fun, and one of the biggest Lego Star Wars games of all time.

With Double Fine no longer part of the Xbox Game Studios family, it looks like two of the studio's best remasters will be leaving soon. The remastered editions of Full Throttle and Day of the Tentacle are on their way out, so i
title: Xbox Game Pass Is Losing 8 More Games In October

author: Dave Irwin
description:
The Castlevania series is no stranger to introducing game-breaking relics. Who could forget the Duplicator from Symphony of the Night, which let you reuse Library Cards to warp to the librarian's shop, throw infinite Buffalo Stars to destroy the toughest bosses, and chug endless healing potions, as long as it was equipped? In the same game, the Ring of Varda's stat buffs alone made every fight trivial.

Other Castlevania adventures also had their fair share of items that exploited that game's individual mechanics, so a dedicated Relics menu opens up plenty of possibilities. With over 40 options available, perhaps we'll see a combination of stuff that breaks this metroidvania wide open. In any case, you can only equip three at a time, so here are
title: Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse Relics Guide

author: Dave Irwin
description:
After gathering all three keys by defeating Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse's first three bosses--The Fallen, Joan of Arc, and Medusa--you should then return to the room where Rose fought the first of the bunch. Here, she will place three stones into the door and descend into the Catacombs. This marks the first really difficult area to navigate as it’s long and winding, with plenty of traps and enemies blocking your spelunking efforts.

To conquer this area, you’ll need to get to grips with using Holy Light to phase in and out of Chaos Shards, dodge deadly spinning discs, and fight against some of the toughest regular enemies you’ve seen so far in this metroidvania adventure. T
title: How to descend the Catacombs of Paris in Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse

author: Dave Irwin
description:
For a fan-favorite character, the lack of Alucard in Castlevania: Belmont's Curse may be somewhat surprising. However, those who actually read the intro to Symphony of the Night will know that after the events that led to Lord of Darkness's first demise at the hands of a Belmont, the dhampir went into what he thought was an eternal slumber to rid the world of his accursed bloodline.

However, he's still in the latest metroidvania adventure... sort of. You see, someone has decorated the main hall with a bunch of Alucard's portraits. One of Dracula's talking statues hints that these paintings have a hidden meaning. So we'll go over exactly what they mean and why you need to s
title: Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse Alucard Painting Puzzle Explained

author: Dave Irwin
description:
Having made your way into Dracula's Castle, Castlevania: Belmont's Curse throws a rather huge curveball almost immediately: a long ascent up the Clock Tower. Now, veterans of the metroidvania series will know making it to the top is no easy feat, with these areas typically housing some fiendish spike traps, flying enemies, and large drops.

The Clock Tower in Belmont's Curse is the most devilish yet, with spinning blades ready to slice you up if you so much as brush past them. On top of that, you've been challenged by the Zealot, a previous boss who says he'll only fight you at the summit. Naturally, you want all of Dracula's minions dead, so here's how to reach the Clock To
title: How To Climb The Clock Tower  In Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse

author: Dave Irwin
description:
Castlevania games typically have relatively simple combat. You press a button and a whip, sword, or other weapon usually comes out swinging. It's not usually complex with combos outside of the Lords of Shadow era, with the series typically focused more on exploration than a thrilling set of moves.

Castlevania: Belmont's Curse significantly changes these combat mechanics as Rose has access to seven weapon families, complete with buffs and perks. Each type has four different possible upgrades you can find on your journey, with subsequent weapons recovered from grand chests. To find the best weapons in this metroidvania, you'll occasionally need to think outside the box and fi
title: All Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse Weapon Locations

author: Dave Irwin
description:
Getting into Notre Dame in Castlevania: Belmont's Curse has its challenges. However, the Cathedral itself is home to a giant organ that the Shadow Arcana boss has used to seal himself away from you. Of course, this is Death, and he doesn't make it easy, but finding the ghosts in Notre Dame will give you the three melodies you need to play to unlock the door and fight him.

But what if we told you that, despite beating Death, there is actually a fourth melody you can play? The Shadow Arcana spells hint at another tune, but this time there's no ghost to tell you which keys to press. You'll need to venture into one specific room that's thankfully close to a save room, so we'll explain where to go and how to figure out which keys to press to finish th
title: How To Solve The Hidden Puzzle In Notre Dame In Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse

author: Dave Irwin
description:
Chances are, if you're reading this, you are a little stuck as to how to proceed in Castlevania: Belmont's Curse after falling for Death's trap. After all, that pesky clock is part of the problem, warping Rose to Dracula's lair before she's meant to fight him and leading to a less-than-desirable outcome.

So if you don't want the worst Castlevania: Belmont's Curse ending, you'll need to find a lead. Naturally, with a castle so labyrinthine in its design, there are potential leads everywhere you look. However, one early example you may have seen is a giant painting of Notre Dame Cathedral, just hanging there in a giant hallway. Those who have played Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin might have an inkling of what this means, but you'll need to gather a few key items together before you can explore this hidden area.
title: How To Enter Notre Dame in Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse

author: Callum Self
description:
As someone who has been enjoying the monster-infested streets of Paris (said in a French accent), Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse has made me fall in love with the decades-old series once again. Of course, many of these games were released before I was even born, and chances are, that’s the case for you, too--but don’t worry! You can catch up with this excellent giveaway for a chance to win 19 Castlevania games, two DLCs for the brilliant Lords of Shadow, and a book to boot. Try fitting that in a coffin.

While Belmont’s Curse is the most recent entry, the Castlevania series is full of bangers. The original games are retro goodness, seeing you deal with an onslaught of monsters in frustratingly fun ways. Sure, they have some annoying elements--looking near you, Medusa Heads. Not at you; you can’t fool me. But that’s part of the charm, and the earliest
title: Win 19 Castlevania Games And Two DLCs In This Fangtastic Giveaway
